partitions.heading: The Current War (2017 / 2019)
partitions.subtitle: Film Critique & Technological Assessment by Aloysius Conway

cards.title: Project Scope & Historical Thesis
cards.text: Alfonso Gomez-Rejon's 'The Current War: Director's Cut' dramatizes the late 19th-century infrastructure conflict between Thomas Edison's low-voltage direct current (DC) system and the alternating current (AC) polyphase grid championed by George Westinghouse and Nikola Tesla. This project evaluates the film's technological accuracy, dramatic license, and cultural depiction of the 2nd Industrial Revolution.

partitions.heading: Plot Summary & Official Trailer
partitions.subtitle: The Battle to Electrify Gilded Age America

cards.title: Synopsis (Spoiler-Free)
cards.text: Set in the 1880s and 1890s, the film follows Thomas Edison as he illuminates Manhattan using direct current, backed by financier J.P. Morgan. Industrialist George Westinghouse recognizes DC's inherent transmission distance limits and wagers his fortune on high-voltage alternating current. As Nikola Tesla breaks away from Edison's lab to patent the polyphase induction motor, Edison wages an increasingly desperate public relations smear campaign to declare AC fatally unsafe, culminating in the historic bid to light the 1893 Chicago World's Fair.

cards.title: Director: Alfonso Gomez-Rejon
cards.text: Known for 'Me and Earl and the Dying Girl', Gomez-Rejon brings a fast-paced, kinetic visual style characterized by split diopters, tilted angles, and rapid montage editing. After the original studio release was shelved during the collapse of The Weinstein Company, Gomez-Rejon regained creative control to re-edit and release the definitive 2019 Director's Cut.

cards.title: Lead Cast & Character Portrayals
cards.text: Benedict Cumberbatch portrays Thomas Edison as an obstinate, celebrity-driven visionary whose brilliance is matched by his pride. Michael Shannon delivers an understated, principled performance as George Westinghouse. Nicholas Hoult captures Nikola Tesla's eccentric technical genius, while Matthew Macfadyen plays the ruthless capital interests of J.P. Morgan.

partitions.heading: Educational Value: The Technology Clash
partitions.subtitle: Physics, Grid Economics, and Historical Accuracy

cards.title: Transmission Physics: DC Line Loss vs. AC Transformers
cards.text: Edison's direct current (DC) system operated at low distribution voltages (~110V). Transmitting power over long distances required massive electrical currents, leading to unsustainable resistive thermal losses (P = I²R) and requiring dedicated coal-fired generating plants every one to two miles. Westinghouse realized that alternating current (AC) could be stepped up to thousands of volts using transformers, slashing current, drastically reducing copper conductor thickness, and carrying power dozens of miles before stepping down for household use.
points: DC: Low voltage, high current, heavy conductor weight, short transmission radius.
AC: High voltage step-up, minimal copper gauge, long-distance transmission from remote hydro plants.
Historical Reality: The film accurately captures the economic and physical constraints that doomed standalone DC grids.

cards.title: The Smear Campaign & The Electric Chair
cards.text: Facing commercial defeat, Edison and engineer Harold P. Brown exploited public fear by holding public animal electrocution demonstrations and covertly financing the development of the world's first alternating current electric chair for the execution of William Kemmler. The film accurately portrays Edison's ethical compromise as he attempted to have execution by electrocution termed being 'Westinghoused.'

cards.title: The Climax: The 1893 Chicago World's Fair
cards.text: The turning point of the conflict occurred when Westinghouse severely underbid General Electric to illuminate the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago using Tesla's polyphase AC generators. Powering nearly 100,000 incandescent bulbs without a single failure proved the viability and safety of AC to the global public, directly leading to the development of the Niagara Falls hydroelectric project.

partitions.heading: Entertainment Value & Critical Reception
partitions.subtitle: Analysis of Cinematic Craft and Critical Consensus

cards.title: Student Film Review
cards.text: While 'The Current War' occasionally prioritizes dizzying camera movement over character interiority, it succeeds in making electrical distribution economics visually cinematic. Michael Shannon's performance provides a necessary, grounded counterweight to Cumberbatch's frantic Edison. The film's primary strength lies in avoiding standard hagiography, portraying both men as flawed commercial operators navigating the dawn of corporate capitalism.

cards.title: Critical Consensus & External Reviews
cards.text: The film holds a 61% rating on Rotten Tomatoes (Director's Cut), with critics praising the dramatic re-edit compared to the compromised festival cut. Reviews from RogerEbert.com and Mark Kermode noted that while the historical exposition can feel compressed, the production design and visual scope faithfully capture Gilded Age industrial ambition.
